title: Reading the histogram
summary: Check exposure by shape, not by the screen.

blocks.text: The histogram counts the pixels from black (left) to white (right). The back screen lies in bright sun and in the dark; the histogram doesn't.

blocks.alt: Three histograms: piled left is too dark, piled right is too bright, spread out is good

items: **Touching the right wall:** highlights are pure white and can't be recovered. Darken by a stop.
**Touching the left wall:** shadows are pure black. Fine for silhouettes, otherwise brighten.
Snow, sand or a night sky have their own shapes. A snow scene **should** sit to the right.
On a Canon, press **INFO** in playback until the histogram shows, and turn on the highlight alert.
Shooting RAW, push exposure right without touching the wall: cleaner shadows.
